Thought: The acidity of a compound can be influenced by the electronegativity of substituents attached to it. In this case, we are comparing carboxylic acids with different halogen substituents. The more electronegative the substituent, the more it will stabilize the carboxylate ion through inductive effects, making the compound more acidic.

Fluorine (F) is the most electronegative element, followed by chlorine (Cl), bromine (Br), and iodine (I). Therefore, the compound with the fluorine substituent (FCH2CO2H) should be the most acidic.
